description: ExoPulse is an open-access web platform analyzing NASA TAP API photometry and SPHEREx 102-channel near-infrared sky survey data. It phase-folds TESS/Kepler light curves to isolate micro-flux secondary eclipses at Phase 0.5, extracting day-side thermal emission temperatures and geometric albedos. Powered by a Random Forest AI classifier (ROC-AUC 0.927) for red-noise filtering, ExoPulse features 1-click benchmark presets (WASP-121b, KELT-9b) and structured JSON/CSV research data export.
summary: NASA's SPHEREx mission maps the entire sky across 102 near-infrared spectral channels every six months, returning images of over a billion celestial objects. Identifying faint planetary signals—specifically micro-flux secondary eclipses buried in time-series photometry—remains a major data processing bottleneck. ExoPulse addresses this challenge by providing an open-access web application that connects directly to the NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP API. ExoPulse ingests and phase-folds TESS and Kepler photometry, applies detrending and signal-noise reduction, and profiles near-infrared thermal emission across SPHEREx channels (0.75 µm to 5.0 µm). By isolating secondary eclipses at Phase 0.5, ExoPulse calculates day-side thermal emission temperatures and geometric albedos while displaying an AI signal quality score (ROC-AUC = 0.927) to filter out red-noise instrumental residuals. The platform includes 1-click benchmark research presets (WASP-121b, KELT-9b, Kepler-13b), collapsible physics methodology cards, and publication-ready JSON/CSV data export for astronomers, mission planners, and STEM educators.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS: ExoPulse is an interactive astrophysics web application that combines live TAP API queries with phase-folded light curve profiling. When a user selects or searches any target from NASA's 5,500+ confirmed exoplanet catalog, ExoPulse queries stellar parameters (T_eff, R_star, M_star, logg) from the NASA Exoplanet Archive. It phase-folds time-series flux data, applies moving-average smoothing, and zooms into Phase 0.5 to measure secondary eclipse depths (ppm).

SCIENCE & IMPACT: Observing at SPHEREx's 102 near-infrared wavelengths (0.75 µm to 5.0 µm) isolates planetary thermal emission from stellar reflected light. ExoPulse evaluates Planck blackbody curves across these channels to extract day-side equilibrium temperatures (T_day) and geometric albedos (A_g). An integrated Random Forest classifier (ROC-AUC 0.927) evaluates 11 diagnostic features—including red-noise inflation factors (beta) and detrending stability—to distinguish genuine planetary flux drops from instrumental systematics.

TOOLS & TECH STACK:

- Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS

- Data Integration: NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP API (Sync SQL Endpoint)

- Data Science & ML: Python, Scikit-Learn (Random Forest Residual Classifier)

- Deployment: Vercel CI/CD Pipeline

CREATIVITY & FACTORS CONSIDERED: ExoPulse makes complex astronomical light-curve analysis accessible without requiring local software installations. It bridges raw NASA telemetry with interactive visual analytics, providing 1-click research presets, collapsible physics methodology cards, and publication-ready data export (JSON/CSV).
